links.outcome: Substantive numerical/categorical errors in constrained pipeline versus unconstrained LLM summaries
links.effect: Harness found one substantive content error (0.05%) across 2,067 checks in constrained pipeline, versus about two in five checkable numerical statements wrong in unconstrained baseline.
links.quote: Across the three models (Gemma 4 31B, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-4.1), the harness identified one substantive content error, meaning one that would change a clinician’s reading, for a rate of 0.05%, against an unconstrained baseline in which about two in five checkable numerical statements were wrong.

links.outcome: Traceable evidence-ID on each statement in constrained versus unconstrained briefs
links.effect: Every constrained brief carried a traceable evidence-ID on each statement; every unconstrained baseline brief contained at least one statement with no traceable basis.
links.quote: Every constrained brief also carried a traceable evidence-ID on each statement, as the design requires, while every unconstrained baseline brief contained at least one statement with no traceable basis in the source data.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM summaries against source data via automated harness and independent raters
links.effect: Harness: 1 substantive error in 2,067 checks (0.05%); two raters found no hard errors and soft errors in 8 of 25 briefs (32%).
links.quote: Two raters independently coded the narrative prose and found no hard errors (factual contradictions of the data) and soft errors in 8 of 25 briefs (32%), where information was combined across waves or measures, which the harness does not check.
